data.title: bn-3m62: unsealed-segment classification in doctor authority, and owed-reseal vs lost split for seal-pack-missing
data.description:
bn-3m62. Both questions answered with evidence gathered BEFORE any product code, and one of the two premises turned out to be false.

QUESTION A. THE PREMISE IS REFUTED. A pack-default store writes no artifact at all for the live head. The only two .pidx writers in the tree are SealDriver::seal's non-pack branch (mess-index/src/sealed/driver.rs:456-459, unreachable when pack is set because driver.rs:447-449 returns into seal_consolidated) and the offline mess rebuild-index (mess-cli/src/rebuild.rs:174). Both engine drivers pass with_pack(opts.seal_pack) - engine.rs:3013 roll-sealer, engine.rs:4616 seal_active - and the default is true at engine.rs:2811. Measured: 400 batches, 32 KiB segments, 5 rolled segments sealed plus a live head, sealed/ holds exactly 5 files and every one is a .seal, live and after close and after reopen. seal_active over a live head writes a .seal too. So nothing reads the head .pidx pre-roll because none exists, suppression is a no-op, and bn-1yor's 1.00 files per sealed segment is intact.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is worth the lead's attention. authority.rs had only three Serving values, so the live head fell into LogScan, whose operator text (authority.rs) says the background sealer is owed a seal for this segment. That is false for a head by design - sealed_candidate.rs documents and engine.rs:3068-3082 implements the unconditional head exclusion. Two real costs: a healthy pack-default store could never report the authority finding at Ok (every store has a head), and the permanently-present head hid the case an operator needs to see, a SEALED segment whose accelerator is gone, inside the same served_by_log_scan counter. Fixed by adding Serving::Unsealed plus a sealed row field and an unsealed_segments counter, discriminated by mess_log::sealer::read_trailer - one 100-byte pread per segment, the same fact doctor's own segment pass holds as scan.trailer, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about which segments are sealed.

QUESTION B. Split on the durable quarantine slot. Owed-reseal is the new kind seal-pack-reseal-pending at Warn with state pending-reseal and converges next-open. Genuinely lost keeps kind seal-pack-missing at Error, with state lost and remedy mess rebuild-index added, and the message no longer implies a repair is coming.

Why Warn for the owed arm: verify's own contract for that section says every Error there corresponds to a candidate the next open would refuse and quarantine. With the pack withdrawn there is no candidate, the next open refuses nothing and instead re-seals, and doctor already reported the identical store as Warn with state pending-reseal. verify saying Error while doctor said converging Warn about the same bytes was the contradiction; it is closed.

Why Error stays for the lost arm, and this is the part I most want checked: the severity is load-bearing OUTSIDE verify. restore.rs gates on verify.worst() below Error, spec 07 section 1 and 1.2 name seal-pack-missing as the Error that makes a backup cut identity-complete rather than merely data-complete, and backup.rs includes the pack for exactly that reason. Downgrading it wholesale would let a torn backup pass silently. The split provably cannot weaken the gate: *.refuted markers are deliberately excluded from a cut, so a restored store never has a quarantine slot and a torn cut always lands in the Error arm. a_torn_cut_still_errors pins it, and it withdraws the SOURCE pack first so the test fails loudly if a cut ever starts carrying a marker.

The owed predicate mirrors the engine exactly: engine.rs:4039-4045 marks a segment owed for ANY *.refuted whose name parses to its id, not only .seal.refuted, so a .pidx.refuted dragged along by bn-3qh0's shadowed-sidecar withdrawal counts. A CLI keying on the primary extension alone would report lost for a store the next open converges. any_quarantine_slot_for_the_segment_counts_as_the_reseal_request pins that.

DOCTOR ALIGNMENT. doctor's sidecar-missing told every artifact-less sealed segment it was owed a re-seal. bn-3qh0's own merged test never_reseals_a_deleted_pack_on_its_own proves that is false with no marker. Same split, same words, same state and remedy fields, so doctor and verify describe one store with one vocabulary. Both severities stay Warn in doctor; only verify carries the exit-code judgement, and only for the narrower footer-names-an-absent-pack case.

LAWS. Nothing was suppressed, so nothing needed proving absent - but a_cold_open_of_an_unrolled_store_serves_every_event_from_the_log proves the head needs no accelerator: an unrolled store with an empty sealed/ cold-opens and serves every event and every payload byte off the log, and the cold open writes no artifact of its own. No engine code changed. The log stays sole authority in every new message, every finding names fallback raw-segment-scan, and neither new finding claims data loss.

FILES. mess-cli/src/authority.rs, doctor.rs, verify.rs (surgical - the verify change is confined to verify_seal_identity plus one helper and a hoisted discover_quarantined, so bn-w5my's additive verify_reg pass rebased onto it cleanly), mess-cli/tests/doctor_authority.rs (two fault-injection tests now seal the footer first so they exercise log-scan rather than the new unsealed state - intent preserved, and the comment says why), two new test files, docs/observability.md, docs/spec/07-backup.md.

EVIDENCE. 4 new mess-store tests, 10 new mess-cli tests, all passing. Full workspace nextest after rebasing onto bn-w5my's merge: 1220 run, 1220 passed, 28 skipped. cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean. cargo +nightly fmt --all --check clean. clippy on mess-cli and mess-store introduces no warning in any file I touched (the 7 that remain are pre-existing in mess-index, engine.rs, and two test files I did not touch).

WORTH A SECOND OPINION. First, whether the lost arm should really keep Error given the discardable-acceleration law - I argue yes because of the backup gate and because every other Error in the seal-pack family is bytes-exist-and-are-wrong, but it is a judgement call. Second, whether Serving::Unsealed should also win when a DEGRADED artifact sits over a footerless head: it currently does (only a Present artifact beats it), on the grounds that serving means where reads come from, with the bad bytes still counted in artifacts_degraded and the summary still Warn.
